Definition: from G4314 and G71; to lead towards, i.e. (transitively) to conduct near (summon, present), or (intransitively) to approach:--bring, draw near.
BiblicalUsage: Prosago means to lead toward, to bring near, to present. Peter says Christ suffered that he might bring us to God, and Luke says the people brought Paul and Silas to the magistrates.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that bringing near is the whole work of Christ, and every other bringing in Scripture is only a picture of it.
